items.summary: A local, browser-based review surface: when an agent proposes a plan or finishes a change, it opens in your browser — annotate paragraph by paragraph, comment on diffs, and send the feedback back to the same session as its next turn. An Inbox also collects questions and files from all your agents without keeping sessions open. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and six more agents; dual-licensed Apache-2.0/MIT.
items.title: Plannotator: a local review desk for coding agents — annotate plans and diffs before sending feedback back (No. 1 on GitHub trending this week)

items.summary: A cloud Linux desktop with Chrome and a shell. Add box as an MCP server to Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more, and your agent can open a browser, click, type and run commands on that machine while your own laptop stays closed. 5,000 free credits cover about 50 hours; pay-as-you-go after that.
items.title: box: a cloud computer for your agents — Claude, ChatGPT and Codex drive it over MCP (Show HN, Nov 16)

items.summary: A native desktop app with no bundled inference and no account: point it at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, llama-server, LM Studio, vLLM) and it reads and writes files, runs code and builds spreadsheets and small apps inside a folder. The same interface compiles to WebAssembly, so byob --serve plus tailscale serve opens the live session in a phone browser. Dual-licensed MIT/Apache-2.0.
items.title: byob: a local-model desktop AI coworker, no Electron — Tailscale puts the same session on your phone (Show HN, Nov 15)
